---

## Inspection-Led Philosophy (EPA-Aligned)

Pure Air California follows a condition-based, inspection-led approach aligned with U.S. EPA indoor air quality guidance:
1. **Inspect before cleaning**: Technicians review accessible supply and return ducts, registers, equipment layout, and access points before recommending mechanical work.
2. **Written scope before work starts**: Every client receives a clear written scope detailing included systems, components (ducts, registers, plenums, blowers, coils, or dryer exhaust lines), access needs, total price, and any exclusions. Optional treatments or newly discovered items require separate written approval.
3. **Honest scope and health boundaries**: Mechanical duct cleaning removes settled dust, construction debris, lint, and accessible particulate. Pure Air California does **not** claim that air duct cleaning cures, treats, or prevents allergies, asthma, or medical conditions, and does not guarantee complete odor elimination or fire-restoration clearance after structural smoke damage.

---

## Transparent Pricing Guide

- **Residential Air Duct Cleaning**: Starts at **$299** for eligible residential scopes.
- **Residential Dryer Vent Cleaning**: Starts at **$149** for eligible residential scopes.
- **What affects final written quotes in Los Angeles**:
  - Number of separate HVAC systems / air handlers / zones
  - Duct material, layout, and condition (attic vs. crawlspace vs. rooftop package units; older Los Angeles hillside or split-level homes)
  - Dryer exhaust length, bends, booster fans, and wall vs. multi-story roof termination access
  - Additional components requested (accessible evaporator coils, blower assemblies, plenums, reusable electrostatic collector cells)
  - Multi-unit HOA coordination, parking/elevator rules, or off-hours commercial work windows
- Starting prices are planning baselines for eligible residential scopes, not fixed whole-property packages or wildfire-remediation/HOA quotes.
- Pricing details: https://www.pureaircalifornia.com/pricing/
- Online estimate builder: https://www.pureaircalifornia.com/quote/

## Complete Service Catalog

1. **Residential Air Duct Cleaning** — https://www.pureaircalifornia.com/services/residential-air-duct-cleaning/

2. **Residential Dryer Vent Cleaning** — https://www.pureaircalifornia.com/services/residential-dryer-vent-cleaning/
   Full-path lint extraction and airflow verification from the dryer transition connection through the exhaust duct to the exterior wall or roof termination hood.
3. **Commercial Air Duct Cleaning** — https://www.pureaircalifornia.com/services/commercial-air-duct-cleaning/
   Building-specific HVAC duct and ventilation cleaning coordinated around operating hours, tenant access, and facility requirements across Los Angeles County.
4. **Commercial & HOA Air Duct + Dryer Vent Cleaning** — https://www.pureaircalifornia.com/services/commercial-hoa-air-duct-dryer-vent-cleaning-los-angeles/
   Multi-unit dryer vent stack clearing, common-area HVAC ductwork, resident notice coordination, access planning, and written completion records for HOA boards and property managers.
5. **Wildfire Smoke & Hillside Air Duct Assessment & Cleaning** — https://www.pureaircalifornia.com/services/wildfire-smoke-hillside-air-duct-cleaning-los-angeles/
   Inspection-led assessment and HEPA negative-pressure source removal for wildfire smoke particulate, Santa Ana wind ash, and post-remodel drywall dust in Los Angeles canyon and hillside homes. Distinguishes accessible particulate from damaged insulation or restoration-specialist scope.
6. **Commercial Dryer Vent Cleaning** — https://www.pureaircalifornia.com/services/commercial-dryer-vent-cleaning/

7. **Laundromat Dryer Vent Cleaning** — https://www.pureaircalifornia.com/services/laundromat-dryer-vent-cleaning/
   High-volume dryer bank, common manifold trunk, booster fan, and roof termination exhaust cleaning planned around store hours.
8. **HVAC System Cleaning** — https://www.pureaircalifornia.com/services/hvac-system-cleaning/
   Component-level cleaning for accessible evaporator coils, blower assemblies, air handlers, plenums, and connected ductwork.
9. **Dryer Vent Maintenance Program** — https://www.pureaircalifornia.com/services/dryer-vent-maintenance-program/
   Scheduled recurring dryer vent inspections, lint removal, and maintenance logs for homes, HOAs, apartments, and commercial laundry rooms.
10. **Residential Electrostatic Air Filter Service** — https://www.pureaircalifornia.com/services/residential-electrostatic-filter/
    Inspection, collector-cell cleaning, and return-slot sizing review for compatible washable electrostatic and reusable HVAC filters.

## Greater Los Angeles Coverage & Local Property Realities

Primary LA guide: https://www.pureaircalifornia.com/locations/los-angeles/
Full 54-area directory: https://www.pureaircalifornia.com/locations/

- **Westside & Coastal**: Santa Monica, Beverly Hills, Brentwood, Pacific Palisades, Malibu, Culver City, Century City, Westwood, West LA, Sawtelle, North of Montana, Beverly Glen. Considerations include coastal humidity, marine salt air, canyon wildfire smoke corridors, and multi-zone hillside estate systems.
- **Central & Metro Los Angeles**: Downtown LA, Hollywood, West Hollywood, Los Feliz, Koreatown, Mid-Wilshire, Larchmont, Fairfax, Laurel Canyon, Central LA. Considerations include 1920s–1940s Spanish and Craftsman ductwork, freeway particulate exposure, condo/high-rise HOA access rules, and tight street parking.
- **San Fernando Valley**: Sherman Oaks, Studio City, Encino, Encino Village, Burbank, Glendale, Woodland Hills, Calabasas, Hidden Hills, Valley Village, Valley Glen, North Hollywood, Van Nuys, Northridge, Tarzana, Reseda, Canoga Park, Chatsworth, Porter Ranch, Granada Hills, Mission Hills, Sun Valley, Lake Balboa, Magnolia Park, Toluca Lake, Sherwood Forest, Winnetka, Panorama City, Sepulveda Basin, Deer Lake Highlands. Considerations include heavy summer cooling runtime, hot attic trunk lines, and Santa Ana wind dust.
- **San Gabriel Foothills & Ventura**: Pasadena and Ventura. Considerations include foothill canyon winds, historic architecture, and long multi-story dryer exhaust runs.

## Frequently Asked Questions (Summary)

- **How much does air duct cleaning cost in Los Angeles?**
  Residential air duct cleaning starts at $299 and residential dryer vent cleaning starts at $149 for eligible scopes. Final written quotes depend on system count, access, buildup, and included components. Commercial and HOA scopes are quoted individually.
- **How often should air ducts and dryer vents be cleaned in Southern California?**
  Air duct cleaning is condition-based per EPA guidance (visible debris, particles discharging from registers, renovation dust, or pest activity), not a universal calendar. Dryer vents accumulate lint continuously and require periodic inspection and cleaning based on laundry volume, vent length, and termination layout.
- **Should I clean my air ducts after Los Angeles wildfire smoke?**
  An inspection of accessible returns, trunks, air handlers, and filters clarifies whether ash or fine particulate settled in the ductwork. Smoke exposure alone does not automatically require full duct cleaning, and cleaning is not a fire-restoration clearance.
- **Do you clean apartments, condos, and HOAs?**
  Yes — both individual condo/apartment units (confirming unit vs. shared building equipment and management access) and building-wide HOA dryer vent stacks and common-area HVAC systems.
- **How do I avoid vague bait-and-switch duct cleaning quotes?**
  Request a written scope before work starts confirming system count, exact included ducts/registers/components, total price, exclusions, and separate written approval for any optional add-ons.
